gold_trend_state.label: Trend broken
gold_trend_state.why: The long-term line is lost. BUYING now is fighting the tide - "cheap" can get much cheaper, and most big losses happen below this line. netbenefits.plain_summary: What Zacks says after the 5 November report, in plain language: APD delivered the quarter. Adjusted earnings of $3.61 a share beat the $3.60 expected by a whisker and were up from $3.39 a year ago; that makes four beats in the last four quarters (the one before was $3.47 against $3.36, a 3.3% beat). Sales of $3.56 billion were 12.3% higher than last year's $3.17 billion and 7.2% above what analysts expected, with the Americas doing the heavy lifting (+26.7%) while Asia and Europe came in a little under estimates. The stock is up 29.1% this year against 12.3% for the S&P 500 and rose 14.7% in the past month alone. Even so, Zacks has moved it to rank 3 (Hold): the estimate-revision trend going into the report was mixed, not the unanimous upgrades of August, the Earnings ESP (-0.04%) is flat, and its industry (Chemical - Diversified) sits in the bottom 18% of Zacks industries, which historically drags on a stock. Expect it to move with the market rather than ahead of it. Next quarter the consensus is $3.48 a share on $3.26 billion of sales, and $14.40 on $13.36 billion for the new fiscal year (up from $13.45 just finished, about +7%). For your 787 shares: hold, keep the $1.81 a quarter dividend coming (about $1,425 gross, roughly $997 net to you), and let your waiting sell order at $327.50 do its work above the year's high of $324. The thing to watch is whether analysts raise the $14.40 in the next few weeks: if they do, the rank improves; if the stock keeps climbing while estimates stand still, it is getting dearer, not better.

silver.label: Silver

regime.verdict: BULL (above the 200-day): the daily trigger alone works -- 79% hit rate, 26% of entries drew down >10%
regime.plain: regime matters more than any indicator: above the 200-day average the daily trigger alone works; below it, evidence must arm first and the trigger must come last

weekly.plain: weekly evidence on the underlying. A-D divergence was the best single component in the test (19 events, 100% positive at 60 days); RSI divergence counts when its first low was at or below 40 (<= 30 never happens on these names)

capitulation.plain: volume at least 2x its 50-day average, close in the lower third of the day near the 20-day low, then an up-day within 5 sessions. Capitulation alone in a bear worked 40% of the time; it counts only with the follow-through

band.label: owner monthly LIP support (coincides with the Oct/Nov-2025 swing lows)

support.plain: the owner band / 52-week low is a zone, not a trigger: it scores only once a weekly close is back above it (present in 70% of the good entries, but 56% alone)

volume.note: no volume on this series at TradingView
volume.plain: after a climax, a retest on shrinking volume (20-day average at 75% of the 50-day or less) is the Wyckoff "test" -- indices only; low-volume single stocks underperform

What are the best funds buying?

Which countries and themes look strong?

Is it a good moment to buy (buy now, wait for a dip, avoid)?
Is the trend up, broken or still bottoming?
Is it above its long-term average and not stretched?
Has a falling stock really turned?

Would the stricter bottom check hold this back?
Is the market in an up or down phase?
Has the 50-day or the ATR stop been broken?
Where are metals and big traders leaning?

master_signal.rule: Business engines say whether the company is attractive; price engines say whether the moment is right; a holding takes the exit arbiter instruction first. BUY needs two business votes and a strong price; BUY SMALL needs one and a positive price; a good business with a weak price is WAIT FOR PRICE.

rules.1: Reversal candle at a level: low touches a support zone, closes green, above the prior day's midpoint, in the upper third of its range. Buy a tranche at the next open; the next session must hold that low or no further tranche.
rules.2: Undercut and reclaim: price trades below a prior swing low intraday but the daily close is back above it (the classic shakeout low).
rules.3: Hourly structure turns: on the 1-hour chart a higher low, then a close above the previous hourly swing high (the intraday version, for a US-session add).
rules.4: Volume signature: the low day prints at least 1.5x the 30-day average volume (capitulation), then the next session is a lighter-volume down day, or an up day on above-average volume.
rules.5: RSI with divergence: daily RSI 30-40 at the touch, and price makes a lower low while RSI makes a higher low (the strongest single signal).
rules.6: Invalidation: a daily close below the base floor breaks the base (no averaging until the next level is tested and confirms by rule 1 or 2). A close below that next level is AVOID.
